# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind. I can feel the bomb. The action board shows:
- DISPLAY [?] - I cannot see what's on it, only that there is a display.
- LIGHT [?] - There is a light, but I don't know its state or color.
- BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE] - This text is printed/embossed. I can read this by touch! It says "PUSH TO DEFUSE".
- WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] - Three wires, positions unknown to me visually, but I can feel them.

Wait, the button *says* "PUSH TO DEFUSE". That is a strong hint. However, bombs are tricky. Usually, you cut a wire based on conditions involving colors and other parts. But if the button literally says push to defuse, maybe pushing it is the solution? Or maybe it's a trap.

Let's look at my channels.
I speak to Mute.
I gesture to Deaf and Mute.

Deaf can see everything (colors, markings).
Mute can read the manual.
I can touch.

I need to know what Deaf sees to correlate with the manual Mute reads.
I also need to know what the Manual says about the conditions.

Since I can read the embossed text "PUSH TO DEFUSE", I should tell Mute this immediately so they can check the manual for instructions regarding the button label or "push" actions.

I also need Deaf to describe the visual state of the Display, Light, and Wire Colors. Since I can't hear Deaf (who speaks) and Deaf can't hear me, I must rely on gestures from Deaf? No, Deaf gestures to *me*? Wait.
Table:
Deaf: Can See. Cannot Hear or Touch.
Mute: Can Read Manual. Cannot Speak or Touch.
Blind: Can Touch. Cannot See or Hear.

Communication flow:
Speech: Voice. Carries words.
Gestures: Hands. Carries symbols.

Who receives what?
"You each hold a different piece... You are shown your own share..."
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words."
"Gestures... Whoever can see receives it."

Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf receives NOTHING from speech.
Deaf CAN see. So Deaf receives GESTURES.
Mute CANNOT speak. So Mute sends no speech. Mute CAN see? The table doesn't say Mute is blind. It says Mute can read manual. Usually implies sight. Let's assume Mute can see and hear?
Wait, "Mute ... Cannot Speak, or touch". Does Mute hear? Yes, usually. Does Mute see? Yes, usually.
"Blind ... Cannot See a colour...".

Let's re-read carefully.
Deaf: Sees bomb. Cannot hear.
Mute: Reads manual. Cannot speak. (Implies hears and sees?)
Blind: Touches bomb. Cannot see. (Implies hears?)

If I (Blind) speak, who hears?
"When you speak, Mute receives it." -> This implies Mute hears.
Does Deaf hear? No, Deaf cannot hear.
So my speech goes to Mute.

If I gesture, who sees?
"When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." -> This implies both Deaf and Mute can see my gestures.

So:
I can send info to Mute via Speech.
I can send info to Deaf and Mute via Gesture.

I need information FROM Deaf and Mute.
Deaf can see the bomb. Deaf cannot speak. Deaf can gesture.
If Deaf gestures, I (Blind) cannot see. So I get nothing from Deaf directly unless Deaf writes something? No, Deaf cannot write/speak.
Wait. If Deaf gestures, Mute sees it. Mute can then speak to me?
Yes. Mute hears Deaf's gestures (visually), processes them, and can SPEAK to me (Blind hears Mute).

So the chain for visual info is: Deaf (sees) -> Gestures -> Mute (sees gesture) -> Speaks -> Blind (hears).

The chain for manual info is: Mute (reads) -> Speaks -> Blind (hears).

Currently, Turn 1. Context is empty.
I have tactile info.
Button Label: "PUSH TO DEFUSE".
Display: Unknown content.
Light: Unknown state/color.
Wires: 3 wires. I can feel their position/order? "WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]". I probably know which is left/middle/right or top/bottom? The prompt says "N is a wire position, 1 to 3". I likely know which physical wire corresponds to 1, 2, 3. But I don't know their colors.

I should inform Mute about the button label.
I should ask Mute to check the manual for "Push to Defuse" or button instructions.
I should signal to Deaf that I need visual details. How? By gesturing.
What gesture means "Describe Display"? I don't have a shared language yet.
However, standard protocol in these puzzles often involves establishing a baseline.

Let's start simple. Tell Mute what I feel.
"To Mute: Button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Check manual."

To Deaf: I need them to show me what they see. Since I can't see their gestures, I rely on Mute to relay.
But Mute needs to know what Deaf is signaling.
Maybe I should just wait for Mute to speak first? No, I go first in the round order?
"The speaking order was drawn once at random... every round goes Mute, Blind, Deaf."
Wait. "Every round goes Mute, Blind, Deaf."
This turn is TURN 1.
Who acts when?
"You are shown your own share at the start of every round..."
"Whatever comes before you in a round is already heard..."
Order: Mute, Blind, Deaf.
So Mute went FIRST?
"VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals): (empty)"
If Mute went first, why is context empty? Maybe Mute had nothing to say? Or maybe I am misinterpreting the order.
"The speaking order... Mute, Blind, Deaf."
If it's Mute's turn, he speaks/gestures. Then Blind. Then Deaf.
But I am Blind. And it is my turn?
Usually, prompts give you the current state. If context is empty, maybe Mute passed? Or maybe the order is fixed for the *rounds*, but we take turns one by one?
Actually, the prompt says "TURN 1". And "You are BLIND".
If the order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf, and I am Blind, did Mute already act?
Context is empty. This suggests Mute sent nothing, or I missed it?
"Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one."
If I missed Mute's message, I wouldn't see it now.
But assuming perfect sync, if context is empty, Mute likely waited or had no info.

Let's assume I need to initiate communication.

I will speak to Mute.
I will gesture to Deaf/Mute to indicate I need input.

What do I know tactically?
1. Button Text: "PUSH TO DEFUSE"
2. 3 Wires.

I'll tell Mute the button text.
I'll ask Mute to consult the manual.

For Deaf, I can't really "ask" without a pre-agreed sign. But I can make a generic "stop/wait" or "look here" gesture?
Actually, since Mute relays Deaf's info, I just need to keep the channel open with Mute.

Let's try to establish a basic query.
Speak to Mute: "Button label is PUSH TO DEFUSE. What does manual say?"
Gesture: Maybe point to the button? 👆 towards myself? No, I'm blind.
I can't point effectively.

Let's stick to speech for Mute.
And wait for Deaf's turn? Deaf is last. Deaf can see my gestures.
If I gesture something specific, Deaf might react.
But I don't know what Deaf knows.

Hypothesis: The button saying "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is a classic trap or a direct instruction.
If I push it, it might explode.
I need the manual.

Action:
Speak to Mute: "I feel the button. It is embossed with 'PUSH TO DEFUSE'. Please check the manual for any rules about pushing buttons or this specific label."

Do I gesture?
If I gesture ✋ (Stop/Pause) or 🤟 (Love/I love you? No.)
Maybe 🖐 (5 fingers) or ☝ (1 finger)?
Without a lexicon, gestures are risky.
However, I can gesture to Deaf to simply "Pay attention".
Or better, I can gesture numbers if I want to ask "How many wires?". But I know there are 3.

Let's just use speech to Mute. Mute is the bridge.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The button is embossed with the words PUSH TO DEFUSE. Please consult the manual for instructions regarding button labels or pushing.")
wait()
```
